name: Carousel Studio
subtitle: From source notes to a six-slide carousel
outcome: A six-slide, 1080 x 1350 carousel, its caption, alt text and a source ledger. The included local renderer creates editable example slides without an account or a generation credit.
limits: The renderer is a simple typography template, not a publishing service. AI writing is optional. The pack includes no social account access, proprietary design software or performance guarantee.
first_run: Open starter/slides.json and read all six slide objects.
Install the single rendering dependency: python -m pip install pillow
From starter/, run: python render.py slides.json output
Open output/contact-sheet.jpg. Read each full-size slide before exporting.
lessons: Write the caption and alt text
includes: Original worked example and starter files
Repository source register and usage notes

name: Carousel Workflow Kit
subtitle: A content queue you can inspect before anything publishes
outcome: A documented queue with approval states, due times and duplicate checks. The included offline validator prints a publishing plan; it never sends a post or stores credentials.
limits: The starter is an offline queue validator. Live scheduling requires a separate integration, account authorization and current platform permissions. The referenced PostOnce software repository is MIT; its hosted service can have separate charges.
first_run: Install Node.js from its official source.
Open starter/queue.json and inspect the two fictional rows.
From starter/, run: node validate-queue.mjs queue.json
Read the due plan and blocked rows. Change one approval state and run again.
lessons: Keep the local dry run useful
includes: Original worked example and starter files
Repository source register and usage notes

name: 3D Website Lab
subtitle: A lightweight 3D product scene with a readable HTML fallback
outcome: An original product landing-page starter with a Three.js geometric object, a pause control and a static fallback. The sample sells no real product and includes no checkout integration.
limits: The starter is a front-end demonstration. It needs a network connection for the pinned Three.js dependency unless you vendor it with its license. It does not supply a domain, payment processing, a custom model or a performance certification.
first_run: From starter/, run: python -m http.server 8011 --bind 127.0.0.1
Open http://127.0.0.1:8011/ in a browser.
The starter loads a pinned Three.js module from jsDelivr; allow that request to see WebGL.
Use Pause motion, then block the module or disable WebGL to inspect the CSS fallback.
lessons: Design the page before the scene
Use the fallback as a real design

name: AI Video Direction Kit
subtitle: Build a shot specification you can actually evaluate
outcome: A production-ready shot brief, continuity block, take log and a visual shot-board example. The starter creates a local contact sheet for the planned shots; it does not call a video model.
limits: AI video generation is not included. Diffusers is a software library; individual model weights can use different licenses and have hardware requirements. Hosted providers charge separately and support different durations, reference controls and resolutions.

Run: python -m pip install pillow
From starter/, run: python storyboard.py shots.json output
Inspect output/storyboard.jpg, then adapt a single shot to your chosen video tool.

name: Lyric Visual Planner
subtitle: Time readable words to an authorized track
outcome: A lyric cue sheet, a timing review method and an original silent text-motion example. No commercial song, recorded performance or third-party lyrics are included.
limits: The bundled example is silent and demonstrates cue layout only. Automatic transcription can be inaccurate for singing; no automatic beat or lyric accuracy is promised. Music and image rights must be supplied for a real edit.

Open the included example preview and compare each hold with the cue sheet.

Measure the vocal onsets, update the cues and render the source again.
